The bank's gradient boosting model must be assigning essentially random scores, since consistent explanations are only ever possible for simple linear models
LIME always automatically overrides and completely replaces whatever SHAP reports for that exact same prediction, every single time
explanation: Global, aggregated attribution (SHAP summary) and a locally fitted, instance-specific approximation (LIME) measure different things and can legitimately diverge for a single customer without indicating a bug, a broken model, or that one method simply overrides the other.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: Continuing the same scenario, what can the bank reasonably infer about the model's behavior from the fact that SHAP and LIME disagree for this one rejected customer?
options: The model's behavior for this customer is likely nonlinear or shaped by feature interactions that the two methods capture differently, rather than there necessarily being an error
The underlying lending model has definitely and completely memorized its training data, meaning it must be badly overfitting in general and should be discarded immediately
This particular customer's loan application must have contained some invalid, inconsistent, or corrupted underlying data somewhere
The bank must immediately and permanently stop using both of these explanation methods entirely, going forward with no exceptions
explanation: Disagreement for a single instance is more naturally read as evidence of nonlinearity or interaction effects captured differently by each method, not as proof of overfitting, data corruption, or a reason to abandon both methods.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: Which statement correctly contrasts the theoretical foundations of SHAP and LIME?
options: SHAP is grounded in Shapley values from cooperative game theory, while LIME is grounded in fitting a local surrogate regression model on perturbed samples
SHAP and LIME are both based on exactly the same underlying mathematical theory, differing only in their visualization style
LIME is actually grounded in Shapley values from game theory, while SHAP is grounded in local surrogate regression instead
Both SHAP and LIME absolutely require fully retraining the original black-box model before either one can produce any explanation every single time either one is used
explanation: SHAP's foundation is cooperative game theory and Shapley values, while LIME's is local surrogate regression on perturbed data; the two are not the same theory, the foundations are not swapped, and neither method requires retraining the original model.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: A hospital wants to (1) audit which factors most influence readmission risk across its entire patient population, and (2) give one attending physician a quick, understandable reason for a single patient's elevated score. Which combined approach best serves both goals?
options: Use a SHAP summary (global) plot aggregated across many patients for the population-level audit, and a local explanation such as a SHAP waterfall or LIME output for the individual patient
Use only a single LIME explanation generated once and then apply it uniformly across the entire patient population without any further modification at all
Use only the readmission model's single overall accuracy score to try to satisfy both of these very different audit purposes at once
Use just one single SHAP dependence plot restricted to a single feature to try to satisfy both of these very different purposes at once
explanation: Population-level auditing calls for an aggregated global view, while a single patient's case calls for a local explanation; a single LIME run, an accuracy figure, or a one-feature dependence plot cannot satisfy both needs.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the formal guarantees of SHAP from those of LIME?
options: SHAP's attributions satisfy formal consistency properties such as efficiency and symmetry, while LIME's local regression coefficients carry no equivalent formal guarantee
LIME's attributions actually satisfy formal mathematical consistency properties like efficiency, while SHAP's carry no such equivalent guarantee at all according to its original publication
Both methods satisfy exactly identical formal mathematical guarantees, both of which are ultimately derived from cooperative game theory
Neither method actually provides any kind of mathematically motivated or theoretically grounded attribution at all, in any form
explanation: Only SHAP's Shapley-value basis comes with formal axiomatic guarantees (efficiency, symmetry, etc.); LIME's surrogate-fitting approach does not carry an equivalent formal guarantee, and both methods are mathematically motivated, just differently.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: A regulator asks a bank to demonstrate that its explanation method's reported feature contributions always reconcile exactly with the change in a loan applicant's predicted score. Which explanation approach is inherently better suited to satisfy this specific requirement?
options: SHAP, because its efficiency axiom guarantees contributions sum exactly to the gap between the prediction and the baseline
LIME, because its local surrogate model is always mathematically guaranteed to match the black-box prediction exactly even without a background dataset of any kind
Either method equally, because both are mathematically guaranteed to reconcile exactly with the original prediction
Neither method, because no explanation approach can ever reconcile exactly with any model's actual prediction
explanation: SHAP's efficiency axiom specifically guarantees an exact reconciliation; LIME's surrogate is only an approximation with no such guarantee, so SHAP is the better-suited tool for this precise regulatory requirement.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: For one insurance customer, SHAP and LIME largely agree on the top three drivers of their premium. What does this agreement most reasonably suggest?
options: It strengthens confidence that those features are genuinely driving the prediction for this customer, since two differently-founded methods converge on the same answer
It proves conclusively and beyond any reasonable doubt that the entire pricing model is completely free of bias
It proves that the two differently-founded explanation methods must be mathematically identical to one another in every single case
It means the insurer no longer needs to retain or carefully maintain either explanation method going forward from this point on
explanation: Convergence between two independently-founded methods is reassuring evidence (not absolute proof of fairness), it doesn't mean the methods are mathematically identical in general, and it doesn't eliminate the ongoing value of having both tools available.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: A bank wants to show regulators both that its lending model behaves consistently across its whole applicant population and that any single rejected applicant received an adequate, specific explanation. Which combined use of SHAP and LIME best supports this goal?
options: Use a global SHAP summary or bar plot to show the lending model's reliance isn't concentrated in one feature, plus local SHAP waterfall or LIME explanations for individual rejected applicants, cross-checked where possible
Rely solely on the lending model's single overall accuracy metric score to try to answer both of these very different regulatory questions being asked at once
Generate just one single LIME explanation for one randomly chosen applicant and present it as fully representative evidence covering the bank's entire applicant population

Avoid producing any individual instance-level explanations at all, since purely aggregate global evidence alone is assumed to fully satisfy both of these separate regulatory requirements and no further documentation is ever needed
explanation: Demonstrating consistent overall behavior requires global evidence, while addressing individual applicants requires local, cross-checked explanations; accuracy metrics, a single LIME run presented as universal, or skipping individual explanations entirely would not meet both regulatory needs.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: Which of the following is a practical reason LIME is sometimes chosen over SHAP for a single, ad hoc local explanation?
options: LIME can be set up for one quick local explanation without necessarily requiring a carefully chosen representative background dataset
LIME always computes measurably faster than every single SHAP algorithm variant for every possible model type including every tree-based SHAP implementation
LIME is the only explanation method that can ever be meaningfully applied to tree-based ensemble models
LIME guarantees the same formal mathematical consistency axioms that SHAP provides, but computes them faster
explanation: LIME's lighter setup for a single local query is a genuine practical advantage in some situations; it is not universally faster than every SHAP variant (tree-based SHAP can be very fast), it is not the only option for tree models, and it does not carry SHAP's axiomatic guarantees.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: A hiring model is known to have strong interactions between 'years of experience' and 'degree level.' Which explanation approach is generally better positioned to faithfully capture this specific kind of interaction?
options: An interaction-aware SHAP algorithm, since Shapley-based attribution accounts for how features jointly contribute across coalitions, unlike a simple linear LIME surrogate assuming local linearity
LIME, because its simple linear surrogate model automatically detects, isolates, and faithfully models all feature interactions present in any dataset
Neither method, since interaction effects of this kind can never be captured by any post-hoc explanation technique whatsoever, regardless of the approach used
Both methods equally well, since interaction handling does not meaningfully differ between them in any practical, theoretical, or computational respect
explanation: SHAP's coalition-based foundation is generally better equipped to reflect feature interactions than a simple local linear surrogate, which by construction approximates behavior as locally linear; interaction effects can be partially captured by post-hoc methods, and the two approaches are not equally suited here.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: An audit finds that LIME names 'Income' as the dominant factor in a loan denial, while SHAP's waterfall for the exact same applicant names 'Credit Score' as dominant. What is the most appropriate next investigative step before concluding the model itself is flawed?
options: Check the fidelity of each explanation for this instance and examine whether Income and Credit Score are correlated, since one feature may be acting as a proxy for the other
Immediately discard both explanation methods entirely and simply refuse to explain this particular model's decisions any further at all without ever offering regulators an alternative
Assume SHAP is automatically and permanently correct in every single disagreement it has with LIME, and stop investigating any further
Assume LIME is automatically and permanently correct in every single disagreement it has with SHAP, and stop investigating any further
explanation: The sound approach is to check each explanation's fidelity and consider feature correlation before drawing conclusions, rather than discarding both tools or assuming one method is always right over the other without further evidence.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: When SHAP and LIME disagree about which feature mattered most for the same prediction, the disagreement most directly reflects a difference in ______ rather than necessarily a flaw in the underlying model.
options: the mathematical approach each method uses to attribute a prediction
the specific training data that each method happened to be given
the particular programming language each method happens to be implemented in
the specific operating system each individual method happened to run on
explanation: SHAP and LIME can disagree simply because they define and compute 'contribution' differently; the disagreement is not inherently about differing training data, implementation language, or operating system.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: For a formal regulatory submission, a bank must state precisely how much each feature contributed to a rejected applicant's score, with the contributions summing exactly to the change from the baseline. Which method's guarantees naturally support this requirement?
options: SHAP, due to its efficiency axiom
LIME, due to its proximity-weighted kernel
Either method equally, since both guarantee an exact sum by design
Neither method, since exact summation is never possible in explainable AI
explanation: SHAP's efficiency axiom specifically guarantees exact summation to the baseline-to-prediction gap; LIME's proximity kernel affects sample weighting, not an exact-sum guarantee, and exact summation is indeed achievable under SHAP's framework.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: A customer support team needs a fast, lightweight, roughly-right explanation for a single customer's case and cannot afford to run an expensive background-data computation each time. Which method is generally the more practical lightweight choice for this specific need?
options: LIME, since it can produce a local explanation from perturbed samples around just that one instance without necessarily requiring a full background dataset
SHAP, since it always requires strictly less computation than LIME does in absolutely every context or model type
Neither method can ever be used at all without a dedicated data science team being physically present for every single request no matter how small or routine the request is
Only a full global feature-importance ranking computed across the entire dataset can ever satisfy this particular request
explanation: LIME's lighter, instance-specific setup makes it a practical lightweight choice here; SHAP is not universally cheaper, neither method requires a dedicated team present for every single request, and a global ranking wouldn't address a single customer's specific case.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: A SHAP dependence plot shows that a feature has a consistent global effect direction across an insurer's whole portfolio, but one specific customer's LIME explanation shows the opposite direction of effect for that same feature. What is the best interpretation?
options: The feature may have an interaction effect that reverses its influence for certain subgroups or instances, so a global average pattern doesn't guarantee the same direction for every single case
The SHAP dependence plot must have been computed somewhere incorrectly, since global and local effect directions are always required to match exactly
The LIME explanation must have been computed somewhere incorrectly, since local and global effect directions are always required to match exactly
One of the two underlying models actually being explained here must secretly and silently be a completely different model from the other one
explanation: Global patterns are averages and don't guarantee identical direction for every individual case, especially when interaction effects are present; this doesn't necessarily mean either tool made a computational error or that different models were involved.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: Which statement correctly contrasts how SHAP and LIME each produce a local explanation for one specific prediction?
options: SHAP's local explanation decomposes the prediction using Shapley values relative to a baseline, while LIME's local explanation fits a simple surrogate model on perturbed neighbors of that instance

SHAP's local explanation always requires training an entirely new neural network from scratch, while LIME's never requires querying the original model at all and discarding the original gradient boosting model
SHAP can only ever provide purely global, dataset-wide explanations and has absolutely no local, instance-level explanation capability at all
LIME can only ever provide purely global, dataset-wide explanations and has absolutely no local, instance-level explanation capability at all
explanation: Both methods can explain a single prediction, but through different mechanisms: additive Shapley-value decomposition for SHAP versus local surrogate fitting for LIME; neither statement claiming one method lacks local capability, nor the claim about training a new neural network, is accurate.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: Auditors want to check whether an insurance pricing model relies too heavily on a single rating factor overall, which would raise a regulatory 'no single-feature dominance' concern. What is the most appropriate use of explanation methods for this specific check?
options: Aggregate SHAP values across a representative sample of policyholders using a global summary or bar plot to see whether importance is spread across several features or concentrated in one
Generate just a single LIME explanation for one randomly chosen policyholder and treat it as fully representative of the entire insurance portfolio without collecting any further policyholder data
Compare the model's overall accuracy before and after removing just one single rating feature, with no reference to any attribution method at all
Rely solely on the pricing model's internal hyperparameter settings alone to judge overall feature reliance patterns across the whole portfolio
explanation: A portfolio-wide reliance question calls for an aggregated global attribution view, not a single customer's local explanation, an accuracy-only comparison, or an inspection of hyperparameters unrelated to attribution.

subtopic: SHAP vs LIME Comparison and Combined Use
q: During a model debugging exercise, SHAP flags 'zip code' as a top global driver of a credit model's predictions, while LIME flags it only occasionally, and inconsistently, at the local level for specific applicants. What should this pattern prompt the team to investigate?
options: Whether zip code is acting as a proxy for a protected characteristic such as race or socioeconomic status, given its strong but inconsistent influence across individual cases
Whether the credit model's reported overall accuracy score was mistakenly computed using the completely wrong held-out test set entirely
Whether LIME is fundamentally and permanently incapable of ever flagging any geographic feature at all, purely by design
Whether the SHAP library currently installed on the team's own machine has somehow silently become corrupted or badly misconfigured
explanation: A feature that is consistently important globally but erratic locally is a common fairness-audit trigger worth investigating as a potential proxy variable, rather than pointing to a mismatched test set, an inherent LIME limitation around geographic features, or a corrupted software installation.
